Born in Lambeth, he developed D. Napier & Son into a major industrial company, financing the Lion engine's development and continuing technical work after moving to Cannes.

long_biography.plain_text:
A cycling friendship helped engineer Montague Napier enter the motor trade. Selwyn Edge asked him to improve a Panhard car, replacing its tiller with wheel steering and modifying the engine. Their arrangement divided the work: Edge became the exclusive sales agent while Napier concentrated on engineering and production. Growing demand led the firm to larger works at Acton.

Napier also worked on the small components that governed an engine's reliability. One of his piston patents addressed the different rates at which aluminium and steel expand when heated. His design used metal rings inside a slotted piston skirt to control its expansion, aiming to prevent the piston striking the cylinder wall.

confidence.reason: Independent industrial history corroborates the commercial partnership and factory move; his published patent directly establishes the component design and stated purpose, without claiming an unverified commercial outcome.
